chapter: Reel 1: childhood, first songs, Fats Waller
title: Only child, absent father, and his mother's push for excellence
summary: Johnson was an only child whose mother did everything; she told him to be the best at whatever he did.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Because I'd like to know, were you an only child ...
You were an only child. Well, you know, when they made you, they threw away the pattern.
And threw away my father on top of it. I had very much of him.
No, my mother had to do it all.
Well, it's not too much different
from today, when these fathers get so busy they don't make time for their kids.
You know? It works at both ends of the poles, you know?
All right, well anyway, I'd like to hear about your mother, because she sounds like a wonderful person.

She was the greatest -- positively the greatest. She always said to me if you're going to be anything, try to be good, and try to be the best. Don't just be along with the rest, she said just be the best -- at whatever you do, do it excellently.

This desire for excellence that she ingrained in you at such an early age paid off because I've known you for quite some time now, Jay, and I just see in everything you do is this desire for excellence; there is no half way about it.
